systems.name: Ocean Systems™
systems.role: Global ocean system connecting circulation, depth zones, seafloor geology, atmosphere–ocean exchange, coastal habitats, nutrients, carbon, marine food webs, biodiversity, observation, and stewardship.

systemBindings.relationship: Rivers, groundwater, wetlands, floodplains, watersheds, and estuaries route freshwater, sediment, nutrients, and organic material toward coastal and ocean systems.
Wind, precipitation, evaporation, temperature, clouds, and storms exchange heat, moisture, gases, and momentum with the ocean surface.
Atmosphere–ocean exchange, phytoplankton, marine food webs, respiration, decomposition, marine snow, deep water, and sediment connect the ocean with the carbon cycle.
Estuaries form the tidal transition between watersheds, rivers, coastlines, nearshore habitats, and the open ocean.
Seafloor geology, heated water, minerals, microbes, chemosynthesis, and specialized organisms connect deep-ocean circulation with hydrothermal ecosystems.
